deep.reconstruction:
Context: Riemann's 1861 Paris prize essay ('Commentatio mathematica, qua respondere tentatur quaestioni ab Ill.ma Academia Parisiensi propositae', on heat conduction), Pars secunda. The question is when the quadratic form Σ b_{ιι'}(s) ds_ι ds_{ι'}, here the heat-conduction coefficients, can be brought by a change of variables x = x(s) into the form Σ dx_ν^2, which is equivalent to a form with constant coefficients. In modern terms: when is the metric g = b flat?

Setup (previous page): if Σ b ds ds = Σ dx^2, then b = J^T J with J_{νι} = ∂x_ν/∂s_ι. B = det b and β_{ιι'} are the cofactors, so β/B = b^{-1}.

Lines 1–2: the identities Σ_ν (∂s_ι/∂x_ν)(∂x_ν/∂s_{ι'}) = δ_{ιι'} (J^{-1}J = I), together with (1) and (2), give:
(3) Σ_ν ∂_ι x_ν ∂_{ι'} x_ν = b_{ιι'}, i.e. g = J^T J;
(4) Σ_ν (∂s_ι/∂x_ν)(∂s_{ι'}/∂x_ν) = β_{ιι'}/B, i.e. g^{-1} = J^{-1}J^{-T}.

Differentiating (3) with respect to s_{ι''}:
Σ x_{,ιι''}·x_{,ι'} + Σ x_{,ι'ι''}·x_{,ι} = ∂_{ι''} b_{ιι'}.
Writing the three cyclic versions and combining them (the usual Christoffel trick) gives
(5) 2 Σ_ν x_{ν,ι'ι''} x_{ν,ι} = ∂_{ι''}b_{ιι'} + ∂_{ι'}b_{ιι''} − ∂_ι b_{ι'ι''} =: p_{ι,ι'ι''}.
Thus p_{ι,ι'ι''} = 2Γ_{ι,ι'ι''}, twice the Christoffel symbol of the first kind.

(6) Multiplying (5) by ∂s_ι/∂x_ν and summing over ι, using J J^{-1} = I, gives 2 ∂²x_ν/∂s_{ι'}∂s_{ι''} = Σ_ι (∂s_ι/∂x_ν) p_{ι,ι'ι''}.

Next, differentiate p once more and antisymmetrize in ι'', ι'''. The third derivatives of x cancel:
∂_{ι'''}p_{ι,ι'ι''} − ∂_{ι''}p_{ι,ι'ι'''} = 2Σ x_{,ι'ι''}·x_{,ιι'''} − 2Σ x_{,ι'ι'''}·x_{,ιι''}.
On the left the b_{ιι'} terms cancel, leaving b_{ιι'',ι'ι'''} + b_{ι'ι''',ιι''} − b_{ιι''',ι'ι''} − b_{ι'ι'',ιι'''}.
On the right, substituting (6) and (4) gives (my step) ½ Σ_{νν'} (β_{νν'}/B)(p_{ν,ι'ι''}p_{ν',ιι'''} − p_{ν,ι'ι'''}p_{ν',ιι''}).

(I) This yields the necessary condition (ιι',ι''ι''') = 0. The left side is the second-derivative combination plus ½Σ(β/B)·(quadratic in p). It equals 2R_{ι ι' ι''' ι''}, the fully covariant Riemann curvature tensor, written via the metric's second derivatives and Christoffel symbols.

(II) To exhibit the invariant meaning, Riemann forms δδ(Σ b ds ds) − 2 dδ(Σ b ds δs) + dd(Σ b δs δs). The second variations d², dδ, δ² are fixed by three conditions that must hold for an arbitrary variation δ'. These amount to choosing second differentials along geodesics / by parallel transport, so that Christoffel terms drop out. He asserts the result is Σ (ιι',ι''ι''')(ds_ι δs_{ι'} − ds_{ι'} δs_ι)(ds_{ι''} δs_{ι'''} − ds_{ι'''} δs_{ι''}). This is the curvature quadrilinear form evaluated on the bivector ds∧δs.

The next page divides by the squared area (Gram determinant) to obtain the sectional curvature (III). It uses invariance under coordinate change and the vanishing for constant b to conclude that (II) ≡ 0 is necessary for flatness.
errors: Sign of the quadratic term in (I) as transcribed. The bracket (p_{ν,ιι'''}p_{ν',ι'ι''} − p_{ν,ιι''}p_{ν',ι'ι'''}) can be relabelled ν↔ν' using the symmetry of β. It then equals (p_{ν,ι'ι''}p_{ν',ιι'''} − p_{ν,ι'ι'''}p_{ν',ιι''}). But the derivation (left side minus ½Σ(β/B)(p_{ι'ι''}p_{ιι'''} − p_{ι'ι'''}p_{ιι''}) = 0) requires the opposite sign when the term is moved to the left with '+'.

Polar-coordinate test of that sign: b = diag(1, r²), ι=1, ι'=2, ι''=1, ι'''=2. The second-derivative part is 2. The correct quadratic term is −2, total 0. The bracket as transcribed gives +2, total 4 ≠ 0. So either Riemann slipped on the sign or the indices are misread. The handwriting of these subscripts is hard to read, so this should be checked against the image and against the Werke text.

Statement (II): the second variations are only described implicitly by the three conditions. The overall numerical factor and the claimed identity are asserted, not derived on this page. They are correct up to normalization conventions, but no proof is given here.

results.what: Christoffel symbols of the first kind p_{ι,ι'ι''} = ∂b_{ιι'}/∂s_{ι''} + ∂b_{ιι''}/∂s_{ι'} − ∂b_{ι'ι''}/∂s_ι (= 2Γ), and the formula for second derivatives of flat coordinates (6)
results.modern_name: Christoffel symbols / Gauss formula for flat embedding
results.usually_credited_to: E. B. Christoffel (1869); Gauss for surfaces

results.what: Four-index expression (ιι',ι''ι''') built from second derivatives of b plus quadratic Christoffel terms with the inverse metric β/B; its vanishing is necessary for the metric to be transformable to constant coefficients
results.modern_name: Riemann curvature tensor R_{abcd}; flatness criterion
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Commentatio 1861, published in Werke 1876); Christoffel and Lipschitz (1869–70) for published proofs

results.what: Invariant form δδΣbdsds − 2dδΣbdsδs + ddΣbδsδs equal to Σ(ιι',ι''ι''')(ds∧δs)(ds∧δs)
results.modern_name: Curvature form R(X,Y,X,Y) on bivectors (numerator of sectional curvature)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the published Commentatio of 1861 (Werke, 1876), the well-known source of Riemann's explicit curvature tensor formula. It is already fully credited to him; the page adds nothing beyond the known text, apart from a possible sign slip.
